# Project plan

## Start-up phase

Month 1 (January 2027): create a GitHub organisation for the three repositories, with MIT for code and CC BY 4.0 for tutorial content and documentation, a code of conduct, and issue and pull request templates. Publish the draft metadata schema as a discussion and send it to the people listed under Consulted and to the maintainers of quarto-live, learnr2 and tutorizeR for two weeks of comment. Set up r-universe for the package and GitHub Actions for R CMD check. Reporting: a monthly progress note in the index repository and a blog post at each milestone.

## Technical delivery

| Milestone | Deliverables | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| M1, schema, validator, template. January to March 2027. | Metadata schema 1.0. `validate_entry()` and `create_tutorial()`. Template repository with quarto-live, gradethis, the publish action and the r-universe repos setting. Announcement post. | A tutorial made with `create_tutorial()` publishes to GitHub Pages from a fresh repository with no manual steps. The template page loads a Bioconductor package from bioc.r-universe.dev in Chrome, Firefox and Safari. |
| M2, index site and reference tutorials. April to June 2027. | Index repository with validation action, nightly build, weekly link check and staleness rule. Site with filters. `tutorial_search()`. Three reference tutorials: introductory R from r-for-beginners, DESeq2 companion to bioc-rnaseq, package development with usethis and devtools. | The three tutorials are listed, pass validation, and their exercises grade in the browser. A pull request with a broken entry fails the check with a message that names the field. |
| M3, seeding and documentation. July to August 2027. | 50 entries for existing tutorials sent to their authors. Author guide, reviewer checklist adapted from the Carpentries Lab, and a page on accessibility basics. Delivery post. | At least 50 entries merged. At least five tutorials by other authors use the template. |

Target dates: schema and template by 31 March 2027, index live by 30 June 2027, 50 entries by 31 August 2027.

Failure modes and recovery. If quarto-live changes its exercise syntax, the template pins a version and updates by pull request, and existing tutorials keep working because each carries its own copy of the extension. If authors do not respond to seed pull requests, entries for openly licensed tutorials are merged with the author named and a note that the author has not yet confirmed, and the author can edit or remove them at any time. If a Bioconductor package has no WebAssembly build, the reference tutorial documents the workaround (a smaller example dataset or a precomputed object) and the index entry records the limitation.

## Other aspects

MIT license for code, CC BY 4.0 for content. All three repositories public from day one. The package on r-universe and submitted to CRAN at milestone 2. Announcement and delivery posts offered to the R Consortium blog. Posts to the Bioconductor support site, the Carpentries community forum and the R-Ladies and rOpenSci community channels. A lightning talk at useR! 2027 at my own cost.

## Budget & funding plan

Total request: 10,000 USD. All labor at 50 USD per hour, 200 hours. No hardware, cloud, travel or fees. GitHub Actions and Pages are free for public repositories.

| Milestone | Hours | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| M1, schema, validator, template | 70 | 3,500 |
| M2, index site and reference tutorials | 90 | 4,500 |
| M3, seeding and documentation | 40 | 2,000 |

If the ISC funds part of the request, M1 stands alone: authors get a working publishing template and a validated metadata file before an index exists.
